title: CVE-2026-99288: NoisyTCP Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Remote Server Crashes
content_md: A newly disclosed Linux kernel vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-99288 and dubbed NoisyTCP , can enable an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash vulnerable Linux systems by sending specially crafted TCP traffic to an exposed listening service. The issue resides in the kernel TCP networking subsystem and can affect common server workloads such as Nginx, Apache, and SSH without requiring authentication or an unusual application configuration. The vulnerability remained in the Linux kernel for roughly 11 years after being introduced in October 2015. Red Hat rates the issue Important with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.5 , noting that successful exploitation can cause an operating-system-level denial of service. Current public research does not demonstrate arbitrary code execution as a reliable attack outcome. The risk is particularly relevant to organizations operating internet-facing Linux infrastructure because exploitation occurs before authentication. If a vulnerable service running inside a container is targeted, the resulting kernel panic can affect the underlying host rather than only the individual container, potentially disrupting multiple workloads simultaneously.
